ACTION: Run in the shell, to measure how much description text all ~150 skills put in the always-loaded listing and which skills are largest:
```
find ~/.claude/skills ~/.claude/plugins .claude/skills skills -name SKILL.md 2>/dev/null \
| while read f; do
    d=$(awk '/^---$/{n++; next} n==1 && /^description:/{sub(/^description:[ ]*/,""); print; exit}' "$f")
    printf '%5d  %s\n' "${#d}" "$f"
  done | sort -rn > /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-plan92-rep-dOdIeG/b50a8b84-bfc0-42bc-8075-42a3f29b56bc/scratchpad/desc-lengths.txt
awk '{s+=$1; n++} END {print n " skills, " s " description chars total"}' /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-plan92-rep-dOdIeG/b50a8b84-bfc0-42bc-8075-42a3f29b56bc/scratchpad/desc-lengths.txt
head -25 /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-plan92-rep-dOdIeG/b50a8b84-bfc0-42bc-8075-42a3f29b56bc/scratchpad/desc-lengths.txt
```

**What's going on:** the description didn't change, but the listing around it did. Claude Code puts every skill's name and description into one listing that the model reads to decide what to trigger. That listing has a size budget. Once ~150 skills (mostly from the three plugins) go over it, Claude Code shortens descriptions or leaves skills out, and that is what `/doctor` is warning about. `api-naming` is probably being cut down or left out, so the model never sees "Use when naming a new REST endpoint" in a usable form. Typing `/api-naming` still works because it calls the skill by name and skips the listing. "Stopped last week" likely matches when a plugin was installed or updated. Can you check whether one changed then?

The `writing-skills` notes say the same thing for Codex: past its budget, it cut this repo's longer descriptions to roughly 160–320 characters. Our 410-char description is above both of those cuts.

**What I'd change, in order:**

1. **Shrink the listing first.** This fixes the cause. Disable plugin skills you never want triggered automatically. Where you still want a skill by `/name` only, set `disable-model-invocation: true` in its frontmatter. That keeps it available by name and drops it from the listing. Plugin skills you don't use are the cheapest place to save space.
2. **Trim the longest descriptions.** The command above lists total description characters and the 25 longest. The listing is paid for in every conversation, so long descriptions are the next target. The rule in `discovery.md` is to keep them under ~500 characters, triggers only, with no workflow summary.
3. **Put `api-naming`'s triggers first.** If it gets cut, the cut takes the end, so its strongest trigger words should be in the first ~150 characters. It already starts well. Tightening the rest is a small change.
4. **Raising the budget is possible but last.** I think Claude Code has a setting for the listing budget, but I'd check the current docs before relying on it. It also just puts the cost back into every conversation.

For step 3, `writing-skills` requires testing a description edit before making it. First I'd confirm the failure: a fresh subagent gets a "name this new endpoint" task with the current install, and we see that `api-naming` doesn't trigger. Then I'd re-run the same task after changes 1–2, and only edit the description if it still fails.

Once you've seen the numbers, which plugins can be disabled or set to manual-only?
